title: NASA: This El Niño May Rival the 1997 Giant
paragraphs: El Niño is a warm period in the Pacific Ocean that changes the weather around the world. It usually comes every two to seven years. NASA says the new El Niño of 2026 is getting stronger very fast.

NASA scientists compared satellite data from 35 years. The satellites measure the height of the sea. The pictures from 1997 and October 2026 look very similar, because the high, warm water reaches the coast of South America.

The American weather agency NOAA says there is an 83 percent chance of a strong or very strong El Niño in the first three months of 2027. This may bring heavy rain and floods to some places, but scientists cannot say exactly where.
